justification: THE HEADLINE IS THE OLD BEHAVIOUR: when the bushfire overlay was empty and the RFS live fallback RAISED, climate_risk_score served 'Bushfire Prone Land: No' at confidence 'high' — a verdict about data the check never received (the DQ-36 class) on a safety-adjacent claim, rendered verbatim as a badge in the climate tool (ClimateRiskResultCard.tsx:173,176). This diff fixes that path and makes every hazard confidence carry a named reason. It also ships the absence-semantics census (item 0, report only) and an observation-mode confidence lint (item 2, never blocks, not wired).

falsifiable_check.passes_when: every reachable normalizer path (15 enumerated across the failure matrix, incl. RFS raise / RFS clear / RFS prone / no-coords) attaches a non-empty confidence_reason; the RFS-failure path yields available=False, confidence 'low', detail 'could not be determined', and a reason naming the failure
falsifiable_check.fails_when: any path emits a confidence without a named reason (the all-paths sweep asserts reason non-empty per path), or the fallback-failure path can again claim 'high' or serve detail 'Bushfire Prone Land: No'
falsifiable_check.demonstrated_failing: TestConfidenceCarriesReason fails on the pre-change code two ways: confidence_reason did not exist (AttributeError/empty), and test_bushfire_rfs_failure_is_not_a_confident_no pins the exact old defect — patch(_query_rfs_bfpl, side_effect=RuntimeError) returned confidence='high', detail 'Bushfire Prone Land: No', available=True on the old branch `"high" if hits else ("medium" if present else "high")`.
falsifiable_check.mutation_evidence: Revert the rfs_state 'failed' arm to confidence='high' -> test_bushfire_rfs_failure_is_not_a_confident_no fails on three separate assertions (confidence, available, detail). Blank any one normalizer's confidence_reason -> test_every_path_names_its_reason names the hazard. Drop confidence_reason from to_dict -> test_confidence_reason_serialised_in_to_dict KeyErrors.

pre_impl.existing_data: No DB writes. Code paths only: services/climate_risk_score.py normalizers; consumers verified before change — climate_risk_pipeline.py POST /climate-risk serves to_dict() to the free climate tool; intelligence_brief.py ingests via ClimateHazardOutput with extra='ignore' (brief seam safe, intelligence_brief.py:725-758).
pre_impl.assumption_mismatch: If _query_rfs_bfpl changes shape, the 'clear' branch still only fires on an explicit non-prone result; any raise lands in 'failed' (fail closed). Composite already rescales around available=False (climate_risk_score.py:417-425, the heat precedent), so an unavailable bushfire cannot skew the score as silent 0-risk.
pre_impl.new_vs_existing: Behaviour changes ONLY on the previously-broken paths (RFS failed / no coords): those now serve could-not-be-determined at low confidence and leave the composite denominator. Overlay-hit, live-prone and live-clear paths keep their prior confidence/present/raw values (existing 66-test file still green).
pre_impl.external_source_error: RFS API raise -> rfs_state='failed' -> available=False + reason naming the failure. Previously swallowed into a confident 'No'.
pre_impl.frontend_type: None required: card renders h.detail and h.confidence as strings (ClimateRiskResultCard.tsx:173,176); confidence_reason is additive JSON the card ignores. RESIDUAL (flagged, not fixed — claim-language boundary): the Present/'Not present' chip (:165-170) still reads 'Not present' for an undetermined hazard because the card does not read `available`; and confidence_reason is not yet rendered. Both belong to the typed-absence design phase.
pre_impl.user_failure_mode: After: the failed state renders 'Bushfire Prone Land: could not be determined' + 'Confidence: low' — never blank, never 'No'. Verified against the card's render expressions cited above.

functions.name: _normalize_bushfire
functions.input: overlays dict from _query_spatial_overlays plus optional lat/lng used only for the RFS live fallback query
functions.output: HazardScore whose confidence/available/detail/reason are decided by the tracked rfs_state (not_needed | prone | clear | failed | skipped)
functions.if_none: empty overlays with no coords -> 'skipped' arm: available=False, low, reason says the check could not run — never a confident No

functions.name: scan
functions.input: repo tree under services/scripts/enrichment/src/frontend-nextjs, .py/.ts/.tsx files read best-effort
functions.output: finding dicts categorised prod/computed/test with file:line, literal, enclosing function
functions.if_none: unreadable files skipped silently by design (observation mode reports what it can read; exit 0 always)

values.nullable: no — always one of five literals
values.guard_at: the if/elif chain at :278-304 covers all five; the else arm is the fail-closed default
values.if_missing: not possible (initialised before the branch); an unknown state falls into the fail-closed else arm

values.nullable: dataclass default '' — the test sweep asserts non-empty on every reachable path
values.if_missing: card ignores the extra key (renders as before); the brief seam ignores it (extra='ignore')

queries.purpose: hazard overlay point query (unchanged by this diff; listed because the normalizers consume it)
queries.where_clause: layer_type = ANY(%s) AND ST_Intersects(geom, point) — no is_current column exists on spatial_overlays hazard layers
queries.if_zero: empty per-layer lists -> each normalizer's absent arm; bushfire now disambiguates via the RFS fallback outcome instead of claiming high
queries.if_wrong: wrong-layer rows would mis-score a hazard; out of scope here (no query change in this diff)
